newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels in big counter attack on troops.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels in big counter attack on troops.

text.p: Tamil Tiger separatists launched a big counter-attack on Sri Lankan troops in the northern Wanni region late on Tuesday, military officials in the north said on Wednesday.

They said a large number of Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels attacked the troops near northern Periyamadu, from where a military column had resumed its operation against the separatists on Monday.
"There was a counter-attack last night, but the situation is now under control," a Defence Ministry spokesman said in Colombo.
No other details were immediately available.

Troops resumed Operation "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", on Monday in an attempt to open a key highway linking the government-held town of Vavuniya to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.
Vavuniya lies some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
Two weeks ago, the rebels mounted a surprise attack on the military's rear near Vavuniya, delaying the main offensive.

Military officials said troops moved into Puliyankulam, some 22 km (14 miles) north of Vavuniya in the heart of the rebel's Wanni stronghold on Monday, and were consolidating their gains. The Defence Ministry has said that more than 50 soldiers and rebels have died in the latest push.
The Defence Ministry on Tuesday said only that troops were closing in on Puliyankulam and that they had overcome resistance from the rebels.
The LTTE's spokesman in London was not immediately available for comment.
But a rebel statement received late on Tuesday said the guerrillas had given strong resistance to the army and had destroyed three of their tanks.
Some 20,000 troops launched the offensive last month to open the highway to Jaffna peninsula.
Jaffna city was controlled by the rebels for nearly a decade before being captured by government forces last year.
The rebels, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east, have now set up their base in the Wanni.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
